CANONICAL_NAME.value: Spacewar! 2B (25 March 1962) -- Steve Russell et al., MIT, for the DEC PDP-1

VERSION.value: spacewar 2b, 25 Mar 1962 (authentic source, as published by masswerk.at)

value.lineage: Written in 1961-62 by Steve Russell, Martin Graetz, Wayne Wiitanen and others on MIT's PDP-1, with the starfield (Expensive Planetarium) by Peter Samson and gravity by Dan Edwards. Two ships under player control orbit a central star; thrust, rotation, torpedoes and hyperspace are computed in real time on an 18-bit machine with 4096 words of core and a Type 30 point-plotting CRT. Widely held to be the first widely distributed digital video game. The body preserved here is the AUTHENTIC 25 Mar 1962 assembly listing, not the later reconstructed-from-binary variant, which masswerk publishes separately.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: real-time interactive simulation on a machine with no OS and no spare cycles

value.built_to: demonstrate what an interactive computer with a CRT could do, by making two human-controlled ships duel under real gravity in real time
value.pressure: 18-bit words, 4096 words of core, no floating point, no operating system, and a display that must be refreshed by the program itself while the game logic runs
value.success_means: the simulation stays responsive and the orbits remain believable within the machine's cycle budget

value.pressure: scarce core, scarce cycles, program-refreshed display, no floating point
value.failure_condition: the display flickers or the game slows as object count rises; integer overflow distorts the orbits

evidence.ref: Graetz, The Origin of Spacewar, Creative Computing 1981
evidence.says: Describes Spacewar's creation on the PDP-1 at MIT and its spread to other PDP-1 installations; the program is tied to that machine and its display.
Spacewar is demonstrated on a restored PDP-1 because the machine it requires is no longer in ordinary existence; roughly 53 PDP-1s were built.

environment.runner: docker prometheus-fossil-pdp1:display (open-simh pdp1 a1f57fa3 with SDL2 video + xvfb; simtools macro1 2d9a2d96), 2026-09-16; the headless :bookworm world is the negative control
environment.world_status: BEHAVIOR_REPRODUCED (2026-09-16, TECHNE-87b): with the Type 30 DPY device enabled under xvfb the 1962 program runs past its display I/O and draws -- frames 300k steps apart show the heavy star and both ships (85 and 120 lit pixels of 512x512, frames differ); with DPY disabled it stops at the IOH after its first display instruction. Frames kept under behaviour/ with their sha256 in the receipt. Run-to-run frame bytes vary (the program's random walk); the coordinate is the lit-pixel band and frame difference, not a fixed image.
